newsitem.title: USA: Western Resources buying Kansas City P&L.
newsitem.headline: Western Resources buying Kansas City P&L.

text.p: Western Resources Inc. will buy Kansas City Power & Light Co. in a $2 billion stock swap, the two companies announced Friday, in the first hostile takeover of a U.S. utility.
Under the tax-free deal, Kansas City, Mo.-based Kansas City Power shareholders will receive $32 worth of Topeka, Kan.-based Western Resources' common stock for each share they hold.

Kansas City Power's surrender ended a 10-month battle in which UtiliCorp United Inc., also headquartered in Kansas City, saw its friendly pact to merge with Kansas City fall apart after shareholders in September rejected that proposed $1.7 billion deal.
Analysts have said the merger of Western Resources and Kansas City Power would create a Midwestern electric and natural gas powerhouse better poised to compete in the deregulating utility business.
The merged company will have nearly $3 billion in annual revenues and nearly 2.5 million gas and electric customers. Western Resources also has 430,000 security customers.
Kansas City Power Chairman Drue Jennings said the deal was expected to save $1 billion over 10 years, but said both companies had promised no employees would be laid off as a result of the merger.

"... This combination will create value for shareowners and choices for customers as we position ourselves to be a premier energy and security provider throughout the nation," Jennings said in a statement.
Under the deal, Western Resources Chairman John Hayes will remain chairman and chief executive of the new company while Jennings will become vice chairman.
Kansas City Power will continue to have its own board and will retain its current headquarters, the companies said.

The deal is subject to approval by both companies' shareholders, utility regulatory bodies in Missouri and Kansas, the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, Western Resources and Kansas City Power said.
Kansas City Power stock rose 37.5 cents to $29.125, but Western Resources stock dropped 25 cents to $30.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
